name: Bill Gates
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Microsoft and secured an early software deal for the Altair
starting_point: Born in Seattle, Washington to an attorney father and a mother who was a teacher and corporate board member; raised in an upper-middle-class family and sent to Lakeside School, an elite private school.
current_position: Co-founder of Microsoft and co-chair of the Gates Foundation; net worth approximately $107 billion as of early 2026; resides in Seattle, Washington.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at Lakeside School and discovered programming
trajectory.description: Began programming on a teletype terminal at Lakeside School, an elite private school in Seattle, where he met Paul Allen and developed an early passion for computing.

trajectory.title: Founded Traf-O-Data with Paul Allen
trajectory.description: Formed a venture with Paul Allen to build traffic-flow counters based on the Intel 8008 processor, gaining early business and engineering experience.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Microsoft and sold BASIC for the Altair 8800
trajectory.description: Dropped out of Harvard to co-found Micro-Soft with Paul Allen, developing and selling a BASIC interpreter for the MITS Altair 8800, one of the first personal computers.

trajectory.title: Licensed MS-DOS to IBM
trajectory.description: Microsoft incorporated and licensed the MS-DOS operating system to IBM for its personal computer, establishing the foundation for Microsoft's dominance in PC software.

trajectory.title: Microsoft IPO
trajectory.description: Microsoft went public, making Gates a billionaire and establishing the company as a major player in the technology industry.

trajectory.title: Became the world's richest person
trajectory.description: Forbes named Gates the world's wealthiest person with a fortune of $12.9 billion, a position he would hold for much of the next two decades.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as CEO and co-founded the Gates Foundation
trajectory.description: Resigned as Microsoft CEO, succeeded by Steve Ballmer, and co-founded the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation to focus on global health and education philanthropy.

trajectory.title: Transitioned from day-to-day role at Microsoft
trajectory.description: Stepped down as chief software architect to devote himself full-time to the Gates Foundation, though he remained chairman of the board.

trajectory.title: Resigned from Microsoft board
trajectory.description: Stepped down from the Microsoft board of directors to focus on philanthropic work, ending his formal role at the company he co-founded.

name: Steve Jobs
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Apple and began selling the Apple I
starting_point: Born in San Francisco and adopted by Paul and Clara Jobs, a machinist and an accountant; raised in Mountain View, California in a working-class family in the heart of Silicon Valley.
current_position: Died on October 5, 2011 at age 56 from pancreatic cancer; final role: CEO and chairman of Apple Inc.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at Reed College and dropped out
trajectory.description: Began studying at Reed College in Portland, Oregon, but dropped out after one semester, continuing to audit classes including calligraphy that later influenced Apple's typography.

trajectory.title: Worked at Atari and traveled to India
trajectory.description: Took a technician job at Atari in Sunnyvale and traveled to India seeking spiritual enlightenment, later studying Zen Buddhism.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Apple Computer Company
trajectory.description: Co-founded Apple with Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne in the Jobs family garage, selling the Apple I personal computer kit for $666.66.

trajectory.title: Apple incorporated and launched Apple II
trajectory.description: Apple incorporated with venture backing from Mike Markkula, and the Apple II was introduced, becoming one of the first highly successful mass-produced microcomputers.

trajectory.title: Apple went public
trajectory.description: Apple's IPO brought the company's market value to $1.2 billion on its first trading day, making Jobs worth approximately $239 million.

trajectory.title: Left Apple and founded NeXT
trajectory.description: After a power struggle with the Apple board and CEO John Sculley, Jobs departed Apple and founded NeXT, a computer platform development company.

trajectory.title: Acquired Pixar
trajectory.description: Purchased the computer graphics division of Lucasfilm, spinning it off as Pixar, which would later produce the first computer-animated feature film, Toy Story.

trajectory.title: Returned to Apple as CEO
trajectory.description: Apple acquired NeXT, bringing Jobs back to the company he co-founded; he became interim CEO and led Apple's dramatic turnaround from near-bankruptcy.

trajectory.title: Launched the iPhone
trajectory.description: Introduced the iPhone at Macworld, revolutionizing the mobile phone industry and establishing Apple as the most valuable technology company in the world.

trajectory.title: Died of pancreatic cancer
trajectory.description: Jobs died on October 5, 2011, after a long battle with pancreatic neuroendocrine cancer, having transformed multiple industries including computing, music, phones, and animation.

name: Steve Wozniak
milestone_by_age_26: Designed the Apple I, the core technical artifact behind Apple
starting_point: Born in San Jose, California to a Lockheed Martin engineer father; grew up in a middle-class family in the heart of Silicon Valley with early exposure to electronics.
current_position: Retired from Apple since 1985; philanthropist focused on technology education; author and public speaker; resides in Los Gatos, California.

trajectory.title: Built first computer and met Steve Jobs
trajectory.description: Designed and built his first computer with friend Bill Fernandez at UC Berkeley, and was introduced to Steve Jobs through Fernandez.

trajectory.title: Started developing the Apple I at Hewlett-Packard
trajectory.description: While working as an engineer at HP, Wozniak began designing the Apple I computer in his spare time, initially offering the design to HP, which declined to pursue it.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Apple and designed the Apple I
trajectory.description: Co-founded Apple Computer with Steve Jobs, designing the Apple I single-board computer that became the company's first product.

trajectory.title: Designed the Apple II
trajectory.description: Designed the Apple II, featuring color graphics, a keyboard, and floppy disk support, which became one of the first highly successful mass-produced personal computers.

trajectory.title: Survived plane crash and took leave from Apple
trajectory.description: Crashed his private plane on takeoff, suffering serious injuries and amnesia; took a two-year leave from Apple to recover and returned to UC Berkeley to finish his degree.

trajectory.title: Left Apple permanently and founded CL 9
trajectory.description: Permanently left Apple and founded CL 9, a company that developed the first programmable universal remote control, released in 1987.

trajectory.title: Awarded National Medal of Technology
trajectory.description: Received the National Medal of Technology from President Ronald Reagan for his pioneering work on the personal computer.

trajectory.title: Inducted into the Inventors Hall of Fame
trajectory.description: Inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame and received the Heinz Award for Technology, the Economy and Employment for designing the first personal computer.

name: Michael Dell
milestone_by_age_26: Founded PC's Limited from his university dorm
starting_point: Born in Houston, Texas to an orthodontist father and a stockbroker mother; raised in a comfortable upper-middle-class family with early interest in business and electronics.
current_position: Founder, chairman, and CEO of Dell Technologies; net worth approximately $100+ billion; resides in Austin, Texas.

trajectory.title: Started selling computers from UT dorm room
trajectory.description: While a pre-med student at the University of Texas at Austin, Dell began upgrading and reselling IBM PCs from his dorm room, grossing $80,000 per month.

trajectory.title: Founded PC's Limited and dropped out of college
trajectory.description: Registered PC's Limited with $1,000 in capital, dropped out of UT, and pioneered the direct-to-consumer PC sales model, eliminating retail middlemen.

trajectory.title: Company renamed Dell Computer Corporation and went public
trajectory.description: PC's Limited was renamed Dell Computer Corporation and completed its IPO, raising capital for rapid expansion.

trajectory.title: Youngest CEO of a Fortune 500 company
trajectory.description: Dell Computer entered the Fortune 500, making 27-year-old Michael Dell the youngest CEO of a Fortune 500 company at the time.

trajectory.title: Dell became world's largest PC manufacturer
trajectory.description: Dell Computer Corporation became the largest personal computer manufacturer in the world by market share, validating the direct-sales model.

trajectory.title: Took Dell private for $24.4 billion
trajectory.description: Completed the largest management buyout since the Great Recession, taking Dell private with Silver Lake Partners to restructure away from public markets.

trajectory.title: Merged with EMC to form Dell Technologies
trajectory.description: Completed a $60 billion merger with data storage giant EMC, forming Dell Technologies, one of the world's largest technology infrastructure companies.

trajectory.title: Dell Technologies returned to public markets
trajectory.description: Dell Technologies returned to public markets through a complex financial restructuring, reversing the 2013 privatization.

name: Mark Zuckerberg
milestone_by_age_26: Launched Facebook at Harvard
starting_point: Born in White Plains, New York to a dentist father and a psychiatrist mother; raised in a comfortable suburban family in Dobbs Ferry, New York, and attended Phillips Exeter Academy.
current_position: Co-founder, chairman, and CEO of Meta Platforms; net worth approximately $220 billion as of late 2025; resides in Palo Alto, California.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at Harvard University
trajectory.description: Began studying at Harvard College, where he quickly excelled in computer science courses and developed early social networking projects.

trajectory.title: Created Facemash at Harvard
trajectory.description: Built Facemash, a hot-or-not style website using Harvard student photos, which was shut down by Harvard administration but demonstrated his programming talent.

trajectory.title: Launched Facebook from Harvard dorm
trajectory.description: Launched TheFacebook.com with roommates Dustin Moskovitz, Chris Hughes, and Eduardo Saverin, initially limited to Harvard students before expanding to other universities.

trajectory.title: Rejected $1 billion Yahoo acquisition offer
trajectory.description: Turned down a $1 billion buyout offer from Yahoo, betting that Facebook could grow far larger as an independent company.

trajectory.title: Became world's youngest self-made billionaire
trajectory.description: Facebook's soaring valuation made Zuckerberg the youngest self-made billionaire in history at age 23.

trajectory.title: Facebook IPO and married Priscilla Chan
trajectory.description: Facebook went public in May 2012 at a $104 billion valuation, and Zuckerberg married Priscilla Chan shortly after.

trajectory.title: Co-founded the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative
trajectory.description: Launched the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative with his wife, pledging to give away 99% of their Facebook shares over their lifetimes.

trajectory.title: Rebranded Facebook to Meta
trajectory.description: Announced the rebranding of Facebook to Meta Platforms, pivoting the company's strategic focus toward the metaverse and virtual reality.

name: Elon Musk
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Zip2
starting_point: Born in Pretoria, South Africa to an engineer father and a model mother; grew up in a wealthy family and taught himself programming, selling his first software at age 12.
current_position: CEO of Tesla and SpaceX; owner of X (formerly Twitter); founder of The Boring Company, Neuralink, and xAI; world's wealthiest person with net worth exceeding $300 billion.

trajectory.title: Moved to Canada to avoid military service
trajectory.description: Left South Africa for Canada against his parents' wishes, obtaining Canadian citizenship and enrolling at Queen's University before transferring to the University of Pennsylvania.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Zip2
trajectory.description: Dropped out of a Stanford PhD program after two days to co-found Zip2, a web software company providing online city guides, with his brother Kimbal.

trajectory.title: Sold Zip2 and co-founded X.com
trajectory.description: Sold Zip2 to Compaq for $307 million, receiving $22 million, and immediately co-founded online banking company X.com, which later merged with Confinity.

trajectory.title: X.com merged with Confinity to form PayPal
trajectory.description: X.com merged with Confinity to form PayPal, with Musk as the largest shareholder; he was briefly ousted as CEO but remained on the board.

trajectory.title: PayPal sold to eBay and founded SpaceX
trajectory.description: PayPal was acquired by eBay for $1.5 billion, netting Musk $176 million; he founded SpaceX the same year to pursue reusable rocket technology.

trajectory.title: Became chairman and early investor in Tesla
trajectory.description: Invested $6.3 million in Tesla Motors, becoming chairman and majority shareholder of the electric vehicle startup.

trajectory.title: Became CEO of Tesla
trajectory.description: Assumed the role of CEO and product architect at Tesla, leading the company through a financial crisis and launching the Model S.

trajectory.title: SpaceX delivered cargo to the ISS
trajectory.description: SpaceX became the first private company to deliver cargo to the International Space Station with its Dragon spacecraft.

trajectory.title: Acquired Twitter for $44 billion
trajectory.description: Completed the acquisition of Twitter for $44 billion, later rebranding it as X and implementing significant changes to the platform.

name: Larry Page
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Google from Stanford research
starting_point: Born in Lansing, Michigan to a computer science professor father and a mother who taught computer programming; grew up in a household immersed in computing and technology.
current_position: Co-founder of Google and Alphabet; board member and controlling shareholder of Alphabet; net worth approximately $334 billion as of 2026.

trajectory.title: Met Sergey Brin at Stanford
trajectory.description: Enrolled as a PhD student in computer science at Stanford University, where he met Sergey Brin and began collaborating on web search research.

trajectory.title: Developed PageRank algorithm
trajectory.description: Developed the BackRub search engine with Sergey Brin, using the PageRank algorithm to rank web pages by link structure, the foundation of Google Search.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Google
trajectory.description: Incorporated Google Inc. with Sergey Brin, receiving a $100,000 check from Sun Microsystems co-founder Andy Bechtolsheim as their first investment.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as CEO, hired Eric Schmidt
trajectory.description: Relinquished the CEO role to Eric Schmidt, becoming President of Products, while retaining board control and strategic influence.

trajectory.title: Google IPO
trajectory.description: Google went public at a valuation of $23 billion, making Page and Brin billionaires and establishing Google as a dominant technology company.

trajectory.title: Became CEO of Google again
trajectory.description: Returned as CEO of Google, replacing Eric Schmidt, to lead the company through its mobile and social era.

trajectory.title: Became CEO of Alphabet
trajectory.description: Google restructured under a new holding company, Alphabet Inc., with Page as CEO, overseeing Google and other moonshot ventures.

trajectory.title: Stepped down from Alphabet executive roles
trajectory.description: Stepped down as CEO of Alphabet, handing control to Sundar Pichai, while remaining a board member and controlling shareholder.

name: Sergey Brin
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Google and developed PageRank/search infrastructure
starting_point: Born in Moscow, Soviet Union to a mathematician father and a NASA scientist mother; immigrated to the United States at age 6, growing up in a middle-class family in Maryland.
current_position: Co-founder of Google and Alphabet; board member and controlling shareholder of Alphabet; net worth approximately $150+ billion.

trajectory.title: Enrolled as PhD student at Stanford
trajectory.description: Began graduate studies in computer science at Stanford University, where he would soon meet Larry Page and collaborate on web search research.

trajectory.title: Co-developed PageRank with Larry Page
trajectory.description: Collaborated with Larry Page on the BackRub search engine, developing the PageRank algorithm that ranked web pages by their link structure.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Google
trajectory.description: Incorporated Google Inc. with Larry Page, taking a leave of absence from Stanford to build the company full-time.

trajectory.title: Google IPO
trajectory.description: Google went public, making Brin a billionaire and establishing the company as a dominant force in internet search and advertising.

trajectory.title: Became President of Google
trajectory.description: Took on the role of President of Google's new products division, focusing on moonshot projects including Google Glass and self-driving cars.

trajectory.title: Became President of Alphabet
trajectory.description: Google restructured under Alphabet Inc., with Brin as President, overseeing the portfolio of companies including Google, Waymo, and other bets.

trajectory.title: Stepped down from Alphabet executive roles
trajectory.description: Stepped down as President of Alphabet alongside Larry Page, leaving day-to-day management to CEO Sundar Pichai while retaining board seats and controlling shares.

name: Marc Andreessen
milestone_by_age_26: Co-created Mosaic, then co-founded Netscape at 23
starting_point: Born in Cedar Falls, Iowa and raised in New Lisbon, Wisconsin, a small rural town; father was a seed company sales manager and mother worked in customer service.
current_position: Co-founder and general partner of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z); net worth approximately $1.9 billion as of 2026; advisor to Donald Trump since 2024.

trajectory.title: Started working at NCSA
trajectory.description: Took a part-time programming role at the National Center for Supercomputing Applications at the University of Illinois, where he was exposed to the early World Wide Web.

trajectory.title: Co-created the Mosaic web browser
trajectory.description: Co-authored NCSA Mosaic with Eric Bina, the first widely-used graphical web browser, which catalyzed a massive increase in web traffic and adoption.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Netscape Communications
trajectory.description: Co-founded Mosaic Communications Corporation (later renamed Netscape) with Silicon Graphics founder Jim Clark to commercialize a web browser.

trajectory.title: Netscape IPO sparked the dot-com boom
trajectory.description: Netscape went public in a landmark IPO that is widely credited with igniting the dot-com era, with shares surging on the first day of trading.

trajectory.title: AOL acquired Netscape
trajectory.description: America Online announced the acquisition of Netscape as the company struggled against Microsoft's Internet Explorer, with Andreessen becoming CTO of AOL.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Loudcloud (later Opsware)
trajectory.description: Co-founded Loudcloud, a managed hosting company that later pivoted to software as Opsware, which was sold to Hewlett-Packard for $1.6 billion in 2007.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Andreessen Horowitz
trajectory.description: Co-founded the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with Ben Horowitz, which became one of Silicon Valley's most prominent VC firms.

name: Linus Torvalds
milestone_by_age_26: Released the Linux kernel
starting_point: Born in Helsinki, Finland to journalist parents from the Swedish-speaking minority; grandfather was a statistics professor who introduced him to computing with a Commodore VIC-20.
current_position: Creator and lead developer of the Linux kernel and Git; fellow at the Linux Foundation; resides in Portland, Oregon.

trajectory.title: Began programming on a VIC-20
trajectory.description: Started programming on a Commodore VIC-20, initially in BASIC and then in machine code, sparked by his maternal grandfather's introduction to computing.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at the University of Helsinki
trajectory.description: Began studying computer science at the University of Helsinki, where he would later develop the Linux kernel as a student project.

trajectory.title: Released the Linux kernel v0.02
trajectory.description: Announced and released the first official version of the Linux kernel on Usenet, initially as a free Unix-like operating system for personal computers.

trajectory.title: Linux kernel v1.0 released
trajectory.description: Released Linux kernel version 1.0, the first stable version, which had grown through contributions from a global community of developers.

trajectory.title: Moved to the US and joined Transmeta
trajectory.description: Accepted a position at Transmeta, a chip design startup in California, while continuing to oversee Linux kernel development.

trajectory.title: Left Transmeta to focus on Linux full-time
trajectory.description: Left Transmeta to work exclusively on the Linux kernel, backed by the Open Source Development Labs (OSDL), a consortium of major tech companies.

trajectory.title: Created Git version control system
trajectory.description: Created Git, a distributed version control system, in response to the loss of free access to BitKeeper, revolutionizing software development workflows.

trajectory.title: Won the Millennium Technology Prize
trajectory.description: Received the Millennium Technology Prize, one of the world's largest technology awards, in recognition of creating the Linux kernel.

name: John Carmack
milestone_by_age_26: Built core technology behind Commander Keen, Wolfenstein 3D and Doom
starting_point: Born in Shawnee Mission, Kansas; grew up in Kansas City, Missouri area; son of a local television news reporter father; showed early aptitude for programming and spent time in a juvenile home as a teenager.
current_position: Founder of Keen Technologies, an AGI startup; previously CTO of Oculus VR; resides in Dallas, Texas area.

trajectory.title: Hired at Softdisk and met John Romero
trajectory.description: Took a programming job at Softdisk in Shreveport, Louisiana, where he met John Romero, Tom Hall, and Adrian Carmack, the future co-founders of id Software.

trajectory.title: Created first Commander Keen game
trajectory.description: Developed the first Commander Keen game while still at Softdisk, pioneering adaptive tile refresh technology for smooth-scrolling PC platform games.

trajectory.title: Co-founded id Software
trajectory.description: Left Softdisk with Romero, Hall, and Adrian Carmack to co-found id Software, which would become one of the most influential game development studios.

trajectory.title: Released Wolfenstein 3D
trajectory.description: Programmed Wolfenstein 3D, which popularized the first-person shooter genre and demonstrated groundbreaking raycasting 3D graphics technology.

trajectory.title: Released Doom
trajectory.description: Released Doom, which used binary space partitioning for fast 3D rendering and became one of the most influential video games ever made, pioneering online multiplayer.

trajectory.title: Released Quake
trajectory.description: Released Quake, featuring full 3D rendering and surface caching technology, further establishing id Software's dominance in the FPS genre.

trajectory.title: Founded Armadillo Aerospace
trajectory.description: Taught himself aerospace engineering and founded Armadillo Aerospace to pursue suborbital spaceflight, winning a NASA Lunar Lander Challenge in 2008.

trajectory.title: Joined Oculus VR as CTO
trajectory.description: Resigned from id Software to work full-time at Oculus VR as CTO, leading the technical development of virtual reality hardware and software.

trajectory.title: Left Oculus and founded Keen Technologies
trajectory.description: Left Meta/Oculus to found Keen Technologies, an artificial general intelligence startup, pursuing his long-standing interest in AI research.

name: Ilya Sutskever
milestone_by_age_26: Co-authored AlexNet and joined the deep-learning breakthrough
starting_point: Born in 1986 in Gorky, Soviet Union (now Nizhny Novgorod, Russia) in a Jewish family; immigrated to Israel at age 5, then to Canada for university; father was a computer scientist.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI); formerly co-founder and Chief Scientist of OpenAI; one of the most highly cited computer scientists in history.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at University of Toronto
trajectory.description: Transferred to the University of Toronto, where he joined the machine learning group and began working under Geoffrey Hinton, a pioneer in neural networks.

trajectory.title: Co-authored AlexNet
trajectory.description: Co-created AlexNet with Alex Krizhevsky and Geoffrey Hinton, a deep convolutional neural network that won the ImageNet competition and launched the deep learning era.

trajectory.title: Completed PhD and co-founded DNNresearch
trajectory.description: Completed his PhD on training recurrent neural networks and co-founded DNNresearch, which was acquired by Google, bringing Sutskever to Google Brain.

trajectory.title: Published sequence-to-sequence learning paper
trajectory.description: Co-authored the seminal sequence-to-sequence learning paper with Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le, introducing the encoder-decoder architecture for neural machine translation.

trajectory.title: Co-founded OpenAI
trajectory.description: Co-founded OpenAI with Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and others, becoming its Chief Scientist and leading research on large language models.

trajectory.title: ChatGPT launched
trajectory.description: Oversaw the research breakthroughs leading to ChatGPT, which launched in November 2022 and became the fastest-growing consumer application in history.

trajectory.title: OpenAI board crisis
trajectory.description: Was a key member of the OpenAI board that ousted CEO Sam Altman in November 2023; Altman was reinstated days later, and Sutskever stepped down from the board.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Safe Superintelligence Inc.
trajectory.description: Left OpenAI and co-founded Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI) with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy, a company focused on building safe superintelligence, valued at over $30 billion within a year.

name: Terence Tao
milestone_by_age_26: Became a full professor at UCLA
starting_point: Born in Adelaide, Australia to Chinese immigrant parents; father was a pediatrician and mother was a mathematics and physics teacher; recognized as a math prodigy at age 2.
current_position: Professor of mathematics at UCLA, holding the James and Carol Collins Chair; Fields Medalist; widely considered one of the greatest living mathematicians.

trajectory.title: Youngest IMO bronze medalist
trajectory.description: Competed in the International Mathematical Olympiad at age 10, winning a bronze medal and becoming the youngest competitor ever to achieve that result.

trajectory.title: Youngest IMO gold medalist
trajectory.description: Won a gold medal at the IMO at age 13, the youngest person ever to do so, after winning silver the previous year.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Flinders University
trajectory.description: Completed his bachelor's degree with honors in mathematics at Flinders University in Adelaide at age 16, having started university-level math at 14.

trajectory.title: Completed PhD at Princeton
trajectory.description: Earned his PhD in mathematics from Princeton University under Elias Stein, with a thesis on harmonic analysis.

trajectory.title: Became full professor at UCLA
trajectory.description: Appointed as a full professor of mathematics at UCLA at age 24, one of the youngest full professors in the university's history.

trajectory.title: Proved the Green-Tao theorem
trajectory.description: Collaborated with Ben Green to prove that there are arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions of prime numbers, a landmark result in additive number theory.

trajectory.title: Won the Fields Medal
trajectory.description: Awarded the Fields Medal, the highest honor in mathematics, for his contributions to partial differential equations, combinatorics, harmonic analysis, and additive number theory.

trajectory.title: Won the Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics
trajectory.description: Received the inaugural Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics, worth $3 million, for his extraordinary contributions to multiple areas of mathematics.

name: Magnus Carlsen
milestone_by_age_26: Became world chess champion
starting_point: Born in Tonsberg, Norway to an IT consultant father and an environmental activist mother; father taught him chess at age 5; grew up in a supportive middle-class Norwegian family.
current_position: Five-time World Chess Champion; highest-rated player in chess history (peak 2882); founder of Play Magnus Group; active in elite chess across rapid, blitz, and freestyle formats.

trajectory.title: Competed in first chess tournament
trajectory.description: Began competing in chess tournaments at age 8, and by age 10 was showing exceptional talent, attracting attention from the Norwegian chess community.

trajectory.title: Became a grandmaster
trajectory.description: Earned the grandmaster title at age 13, the second-youngest in history at the time, after defeating former world champion Anatoly Karpov and drawing with Garry Kasparov.

trajectory.title: Youngest to qualify for Candidates Tournament
trajectory.description: Became the youngest-ever player to qualify for the Candidates Tournament after placing tenth in the Chess World Cup.

trajectory.title: Reached world No. 1 ranking
trajectory.description: Became the youngest person ever to reach the No. 1 position in the FIDE world rankings at age 19.

trajectory.title: Won World Chess Championship
trajectory.description: Defeated Viswanathan Anand to become World Chess Champion, the second-youngest champion in history at the time.

trajectory.title: Achieved highest rating in chess history
trajectory.description: Reached a peak Elo rating of 2882, the highest ever recorded, and held all three world chess titles (classical, rapid, blitz) simultaneously.

trajectory.title: Defended world title vs Karjakin
trajectory.description: Successfully defended his World Chess Championship title against Sergey Karjakin in New York, winning in rapid tiebreaks.

trajectory.title: Defended world title vs Nepomniachtchi
trajectory.description: Defeated Ian Nepomniachtchi in Dubai to defend his world title, then announced he would not defend it again, citing lack of motivation.

name: Lionel Messi
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first Ballon d'Or
starting_point: Born in Rosario, Argentina to a steel factory worker father and a part-time cleaner mother; grew up in a working-class family and joined Newell's Old Boys youth academy at age 6.
current_position: Forward and captain for Inter Miami CF and the Argentina national team; eight-time Ballon d'Or winner; 2022 FIFA World Cup champion; widely considered the greatest footballer of all time.

trajectory.title: Moved to Barcelona and joined La Masia
trajectory.description: Relocated from Argentina to Barcelona at age 13 to join FC Barcelona's youth academy, La Masia, with the club agreeing to fund his growth hormone treatment.

trajectory.title: First-team debut for Barcelona
trajectory.description: Made his official first-team debut for Barcelona in La Liga, becoming the youngest player to represent the club in an official competition.

trajectory.title: Scored first senior goal
trajectory.description: Scored his first senior goal for Barcelona, becoming the youngest-ever scorer for the club at the time, and led Argentina to the FIFA U-20 World Cup title.

trajectory.title: Won first Ballon d'Or and historic treble
trajectory.description: Won his first Ballon d'Or as the world's best player and led Barcelona to an unprecedented sextuple (six trophies in one calendar year).

trajectory.title: Set record for most goals in a calendar year
trajectory.description: Scored 91 goals across all competitions in 2012, breaking Gerd Muller's long-standing record of 85 goals in a calendar year.

trajectory.title: Left Barcelona for PSG
trajectory.description: After 21 years at Barcelona, departed for Paris Saint-Germain due to the club's financial constraints and La Liga regulations.

trajectory.title: Won the FIFA World Cup with Argentina
trajectory.description: Led Argentina to victory in the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar, scoring twice in the final and winning the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player.

trajectory.title: Joined Inter Miami and won eighth Ballon d'Or
trajectory.description: Signed with Inter Miami in MLS and won his record eighth Ballon d'Or, cementing his status as the most decorated footballer in history.

name: Serena Williams
milestone_by_age_26: Reached world No. 1 and won multiple Grand Slams
starting_point: Born in Saginaw, Michigan to a former sharecropper father and a mother who learned tennis from books and videos; raised in Compton, California, training on public courts from age 3.
current_position: Retired from professional tennis in 2022; 23-time Grand Slam singles champion; venture capitalist and entrepreneur; founder of Serena Ventures; resides in Florida.

trajectory.title: Turned professional
trajectory.description: Made her professional tennis debut at age 14, coached by her father Richard Williams, who had trained her and sister Venus on public courts in Compton.

trajectory.title: Won first Grand Slam at US Open
trajectory.description: Won her first major singles title at the US Open, defeating Martina Hingis in the final, and signed a $12 million endorsement deal with Puma.

trajectory.title: Reached world No. 1 and won three Grand Slams
trajectory.description: Ascended to world No. 1 for the first time and won the French Open, Wimbledon, and US Open, defeating sister Venus in each final.

trajectory.title: Completed the 'Serena Slam'
trajectory.description: Won the 2003 Australian Open to hold all four Grand Slam singles titles simultaneously, achieving a non-calendar year Grand Slam dubbed the 'Serena Slam.'

trajectory.title: Olympic gold and return to dominance
trajectory.description: Won Olympic singles gold at the London Olympics, completing the Career Golden Slam, and won Wimbledon and the US Open to return to world No. 1.

trajectory.title: Won 23rd Grand Slam while pregnant
trajectory.description: Won the 2017 Australian Open, her 23rd Grand Slam singles title, surpassing Steffi Graf's Open Era record, while approximately eight weeks pregnant.

trajectory.title: Retired from professional tennis
trajectory.description: Played her final match at the 2022 US Open and announced her 'evolution' away from professional tennis, ending a 27-year career with 23 Grand Slam titles.

name: Taylor Swift
milestone_by_age_26: Released a successful debut album
starting_point: Born in West Reading, Pennsylvania to a Merrill Lynch financial advisor father and a mutual fund marketing executive mother; grew up on a Christmas tree farm and relocated to Nashville at age 14 to pursue country music.
current_position: Global pop superstar; highest-grossing live music artist in history; wealthiest female musician with net worth over $1.6 billion; engaged to NFL player Travis Kelce.

trajectory.title: Moved to Nashville and signed development deal
trajectory.description: Relocated to Hendersonville, Tennessee with her family to pursue country music, signing an artist development deal with RCA Records at age 13.

trajectory.title: Signed with Big Machine Records
trajectory.description: Signed with indie label Big Machine Records, becoming the youngest artist ever signed by the label, and began work on her debut album.

trajectory.title: Released debut album 'Taylor Swift'
trajectory.description: Released her self-titled debut album, which was certified platinum and launched hit singles including 'Tim McGraw' and 'Teardrops on My Guitar.'

trajectory.title: Released 'Fearless' and achieved crossover success
trajectory.description: Released 'Fearless,' which became the best-selling album of 2009 in the US and produced crossover hits 'Love Story' and 'You Belong with Me,' winning Album of the Year at the Grammys.

trajectory.title: Released '1989' and completed pop transition
trajectory.description: Released '1989,' her first fully pop album, which won Album of the Year at the Grammys and cemented her as a global pop superstar with hits like 'Shake It Off' and 'Blank Space.'

trajectory.title: Released 'Reputation' amid media scrutiny
trajectory.description: Released 'Reputation,' a trap-imbued album responding to intense media scrutiny, which debuted with over 1.2 million copies sold in its first week.

trajectory.title: Released 'Midnights' and began Eras Tour
trajectory.description: Released 'Midnights,' which broke streaming records, and announced the Eras Tour, which would become the highest-grossing concert tour in history.

trajectory.title: Won fourth Album of the Year Grammy and concluded Eras Tour
trajectory.description: Won Album of the Year at the Grammys for 'Midnights,' becoming the first artist to win the category four times, and concluded the Eras Tour as the highest-grossing tour ever at $2 billion.

name: Billie Eilish
milestone_by_age_26: Broke out globally with 'Ocean Eyes'
starting_point: Born in Los Angeles, California to actor-musician parents who homeschooled her and brother Finneas; grew up in a two-bedroom house in Highland Park, Los Angeles, in a creative household.
current_position: Global pop superstar with nine Grammy Awards and two Academy Awards; resides in Los Angeles, California.

trajectory.title: Released 'Ocean Eyes' on SoundCloud
trajectory.description: Recorded 'Ocean Eyes,' written and produced by her brother Finneas, and uploaded it to SoundCloud, where it went viral and launched her music career.

trajectory.title: Signed with Interscope/Darkroom Records
trajectory.description: Signed with Interscope Records' boutique label Darkroom in the summer of 2016, beginning her professional recording career.

trajectory.title: Released debut EP 'Don't Smile at Me'
trajectory.description: Released her debut EP, which was commercially successful in multiple countries and established her distinctive dark pop sound.

trajectory.title: Released debut album and reached No. 1
trajectory.description: Released 'When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?,' which debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, making her the first artist born in the 2000s to top the chart.

trajectory.title: Won five Grammys including Album of the Year
trajectory.description: Swept the Grammy Awards, winning Album of the Year, Record of the Year, Song of the Year, Best New Artist, and Best Pop Vocal Album, the youngest artist ever to win the four general field categories.

trajectory.title: Released 'Happier Than Ever'
trajectory.description: Released her second studio album 'Happier Than Ever,' which debuted at No. 1 and showcased a more introspective and sonically varied style.

trajectory.title: Won Academy Award for Best Original Song
trajectory.description: Won the Oscar for Best Original Song for 'No Time to Die,' the James Bond theme, becoming the first artist born in the 2000s to win an Academy Award.

trajectory.title: Released 'Hit Me Hard and Soft' and won second Oscar
trajectory.description: Released her third album 'Hit Me Hard and Soft' to critical acclaim and won her second Academy Award for 'What Was I Made For?' from the Barbie soundtrack.

name: Evan Spiegel
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Snapchat
starting_point: Born in Los Angeles, California to lawyer parents; grew up in Pacific Palisades in an affluent family; attended Crossroads School and Stanford University.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Snap Inc.; net worth approximately $2.5 billion; married to supermodel Miranda Kerr; resides in Los Angeles, California.

trajectory.title: Launched Picaboo (later Snapchat) at Stanford
trajectory.description: Proposed an ephemeral messaging app as a product design class project and launched Picaboo with Bobby Murphy and Reggie Brown from his father's living room.

trajectory.title: Left Stanford and Snapchat reached 1M daily users
trajectory.description: Dropped out of Stanford shortly before completing his degree to focus on Snapchat full-time, as the app reached 1 million daily active users.

trajectory.title: Rejected $3 billion Facebook acquisition offer
trajectory.description: Turned down a reported $3 billion acquisition offer from Facebook, betting that Snapchat could grow independently.

trajectory.title: Became youngest billionaire in the world
trajectory.description: Snapchat's soaring valuation made Spiegel the youngest billionaire in the world at age 25.

trajectory.title: Snap Inc. IPO and married Miranda Kerr
trajectory.description: Snap Inc. went public in March 2017 at a $24 billion valuation, and Spiegel married Australian supermodel Miranda Kerr in May 2017.

trajectory.title: Completed Stanford degree
trajectory.description: Finished his remaining credits at Stanford University and graduated with a BS in product design, 11 years after enrolling.

name: Bobby Murphy
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Snapchat and built the early product
starting_point: Born in Berkeley, California; graduated from Saint Mary's College High School and Stanford University with a degree in mathematical and computational science; grew up in the Bay Area.
current_position: Co-founder and CTO of Snap Inc.; net worth approximately $2.5 billion; resides in Los Angeles, California.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Stanford University
trajectory.description: Graduated from Stanford with a BS in mathematical and computational science, where he was a member of Kappa Sigma fraternity alongside Evan Spiegel.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Snapchat (Picaboo)
trajectory.description: Co-founded the disappearing-image messaging app Picaboo (later renamed Snapchat) with Evan Spiegel and Reggie Brown, serving as the lead developer and CTO.

trajectory.title: Funded Snapchat servers with day job salary
trajectory.description: While Snapchat gained users, Murphy worked as a software engineer at Revel Systems and used half his paycheck to cover Snapchat's server costs until VC funding arrived.

trajectory.title: Snapchat reached 60M daily users
trajectory.description: Snapchat's user base exploded, with users sharing 350 million photos per day by September 2013, establishing the app as a major social platform.

trajectory.title: Snap Inc. IPO and became billionaire
trajectory.description: Snap Inc. went public, making Murphy a billionaire; he and Spiegel held over 45% of total stock and over 70% of voting power.

name: Kevin Systrom
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Instagram
starting_point: Born in Holliston, Massachusetts to a marketing executive mother and a human resources VP father; attended Stanford University, studying management science and engineering.
current_position: Co-founder and former CEO of Instagram; venture investor; net worth approximately $2 billion; resides in San Francisco, California.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Stanford and joined Google
trajectory.description: Graduated from Stanford with a degree in management science and engineering and joined Google, working on Gmail, Google Calendar, and other products.

trajectory.title: Left Google and built Burbn prototype
trajectory.description: Left Google to work at a travel startup and began developing Burbn, a check-in app with photo-sharing features, teaching himself to code at night.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Instagram with Mike Krieger
trajectory.description: Pivoted from Burbn to focus on photo-sharing, co-founding Instagram with Mike Krieger; the app launched in October 2010 and gained 1 million users in two months.

trajectory.title: Instagram acquired by Facebook for $1 billion
trajectory.description: Facebook acquired Instagram for approximately $1 billion, with Systrom staying on as CEO under Mark Zuckerberg's oversight.

trajectory.title: Resigned as CEO of Instagram
trajectory.description: Resigned as CEO of Instagram alongside co-founder Mike Krieger, citing a desire to build something new and explore other opportunities.

trajectory.title: Launched Artifact news app
trajectory.description: Co-founded Artifact, an AI-powered news app, with Mike Krieger, though it was shut down in January 2024 after limited traction.

name: Mike Krieger
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Instagram and built the service
starting_point: Born in Sao Paulo, Brazil; moved to California in 2004 to attend Stanford University, where he studied symbolic systems and earned BS and MS degrees.
current_position: Chief Product Officer at Anthropic; formerly co-founder and CTO of Instagram; resides in San Francisco, California.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Stanford University
trajectory.description: Completed his BS and MS in symbolic systems at Stanford, where he met Kevin Systrom and developed expertise in user experience design and engineering.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Instagram with Kevin Systrom
trajectory.description: Co-founded Instagram, building most of the early engineering and user experience, and the app launched to explosive growth in October 2010.

trajectory.title: Instagram acquired by Facebook for $1 billion
trajectory.description: Facebook acquired Instagram, with Krieger staying on as CTO, helping grow the platform from a few million to over 1 billion monthly active users.

trajectory.title: Resigned from Instagram
trajectory.description: Resigned as CTO of Instagram alongside CEO Kevin Systrom, ending an eight-year run during which Instagram grew to over 1 billion users.

trajectory.title: Launched Rt.live with Kevin Systrom
trajectory.description: Teamed up with Systrom to launch Rt.live, a COVID-19 transmission rate tracker, their first collaborative product since leaving Facebook.

trajectory.title: Joined Anthropic as Chief Product Officer
trajectory.description: Joined AI safety company Anthropic as its Chief Product Officer, bringing his product and engineering expertise to one of the leading AI companies.

name: Daniel Ek
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Spotify
starting_point: Born in Stockholm, Sweden to a nursery worker mother and an IT worker stepfather who gave him a Commodore 20 at age 5; grew up in the working-class district of Ragsved, Stockholm.
current_position: Founder and executive chairman of Spotify; co-founder of Neko Health and Prima Materia; net worth approximately $8.7 billion; resides in Stockholm, Sweden.

trajectory.title: Started building websites for businesses
trajectory.description: Began making websites for local businesses at age 14, charging $5,000 per build and recruiting teenage friends, eventually earning $50,000 in a single month.

trajectory.title: Dropped out of KTH and joined Tradera
trajectory.description: Dropped out of the KTH Royal Institute of Technology after eight weeks and took a senior role at Nordic auction company Tradera, which was later acquired by eBay.

trajectory.title: Sold Advertigo and co-founded Spotify
trajectory.description: Sold his online advertising company Advertigo to TradeDoubler, became briefly wealthy enough to retire, then co-founded Spotify with Martin Lorentzon in April 2006.

trajectory.title: Spotify launched in Europe
trajectory.description: Spotify launched as a fully-licensed streaming music service in Europe in October 2008, convincing major record labels to license their catalogs.

trajectory.title: Spotify launched in the United States
trajectory.description: Spotify launched in the US market, rapidly gaining users and establishing streaming as a viable alternative to music piracy and downloads.

trajectory.title: Spotify IPO
trajectory.description: Spotify went public through a direct listing on the New York Stock Exchange, valuing the company at approximately $26 billion.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as CEO of Spotify
trajectory.description: Stepped down as CEO of Spotify, transitioning to executive chairman while continuing to guide the company's strategic direction.

name: Brian Chesky
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Airbnb and reached early product-market signal
starting_point: Born in Niskayuna, New York to social worker parents; grew up in a middle-class family and attended the Rhode Island School of Design (RISD), graduating with a BFA in industrial design.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Airbnb; net worth approximately $9.2 billion; resides in San Francisco, California.

trajectory.title: Graduated from RISD
trajectory.description: Graduated from the Rhode Island School of Design with a BFA in industrial design, where he met Joe Gebbia and was influenced by the works of Charles and Ray Eames.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Airbnb with Joe Gebbia
trajectory.description: Moved to San Francisco and, unable to afford rent, co-founded AirBed & Breakfast with Joe Gebbia, hosting three guests on air mattresses in their apartment.

trajectory.title: Airbnb accepted to Y Combinator
trajectory.description: Airbnb was accepted into the Y Combinator accelerator program, receiving $20,000 in seed funding and mentorship from Paul Graham.

trajectory.title: Airbnb reached 1 million nights booked
trajectory.description: Airbnb reached the milestone of 1 million nights booked, validating the peer-to-peer home-sharing model and attracting significant venture capital.

trajectory.title: Airbnb valued at $25.5 billion
trajectory.description: Airbnb raised funding at a $25.5 billion valuation, making it one of the most valuable private startups in the world.

trajectory.title: Airbnb IPO
trajectory.description: Airbnb went public in December 2020 at a valuation of over $100 billion on its first trading day, one of the largest IPOs of the year.

trajectory.title: Began living on Airbnb full-time
trajectory.description: Announced he would start living on Airbnb properties full-time, moving to a different city every few weeks to experience the product firsthand.

name: Joe Gebbia
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Airbnb
starting_point: Born in 1981, approximately one week apart from co-founder Brian Chesky; attended the Rhode Island School of Design (RISD), where he met Chesky; grew up with an entrepreneurial bent.
current_position: Co-founder and former chief product officer of Airbnb; designer and entrepreneur; stepped back from day-to-day operations at Airbnb in 2022; net worth approximately $8 billion.

trajectory.title: Graduated from RISD
trajectory.description: Graduated from the Rhode Island School of Design, where he ran the basketball team and met Brian Chesky through shared interests in sports and design.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Airbnb with Brian Chesky
trajectory.description: Invited Chesky to move to San Francisco and co-founded AirBed & Breakfast, initially renting air mattresses in their apartment to conference attendees who couldn't find hotel rooms.

trajectory.title: Airbnb accepted to Y Combinator
trajectory.description: Airbnb was accepted into Y Combinator's accelerator program, providing crucial early funding and mentorship to refine the home-sharing concept.

trajectory.title: Launched Samara design studio
trajectory.description: Launched Samara, Airbnb's internal design studio, exploring innovative housing concepts and prototyping a future house design in Japan.

trajectory.title: Airbnb IPO
trajectory.description: Airbnb went public at a valuation exceeding $100 billion, making Gebbia a billionaire many times over.

trajectory.title: Stepped back from day-to-day at Airbnb
trajectory.description: Transitioned to a non-operational role at Airbnb, pursuing new creative and entrepreneurial ventures while remaining on the board.

name: Palmer Luckey
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Oculus VR and launched a breakout Kickstarter
starting_point: Born in Long Beach, California to a car dealership father and a homeschooling mother; grew up with three younger sisters, experimenting with electronics and VR headsets as a teenager in his parents' garage.
current_position: Co-founder of Anduril Industries, a defense technology company; founder of ModRetro; net worth approximately $2+ billion; resides in Southern California.

trajectory.title: Founded ModRetro Forums
trajectory.description: Founded the ModRetro Forums, an online community for 'portabilization' enthusiasts who modified vintage gaming consoles into portable devices.

trajectory.title: Worked at USC Mixed Reality lab
trajectory.description: Worked as an engineer at USC's Mixed Reality lab while attending Cal State Long Beach, experimenting with VR head-mounted displays and building prototype headsets.

trajectory.title: Founded Oculus VR and launched Kickstarter
trajectory.description: Founded Oculus VR and launched a Kickstarter campaign for the Oculus Rift headset, raising $2.4 million and reviving the virtual reality industry.

trajectory.title: Sold Oculus to Facebook for $2 billion
trajectory.description: Facebook acquired Oculus VR for approximately $2 billion in cash and stock, making Luckey a household name in the tech world.

trajectory.title: Left Facebook/Oculus and co-founded Anduril
trajectory.description: Departed Facebook amid controversy over political funding, and co-founded Anduril Industries, a defense technology company building AI-powered autonomous military systems.

trajectory.title: Anduril reached multi-billion dollar valuation
trajectory.description: Anduril Industries raised funding at a $4 billion+ valuation, establishing itself as a major player in defense technology with contracts across the US and allied governments.

name: Vitalik Buterin
milestone_by_age_26: Published Ethereum's white paper
starting_point: Born in Kolomna, Russia to a computer scientist father; immigrated to Canada at age 6; placed in gifted classes and attended the Abelard School, a private high school in Toronto.
current_position: Co-founder of Ethereum; one of the most influential figures in cryptocurrency; resides primarily in Singapore and travels extensively for Ethereum development.

trajectory.title: Discovered Bitcoin and began writing about crypto
trajectory.description: Learned about Bitcoin from his father and began writing articles for Bitcoin Weekly, getting paid in Bitcoin, which launched his involvement in cryptocurrency.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Bitcoin Magazine and won IOI bronze
trajectory.description: Co-founded Bitcoin Magazine with Mihai Alisie, the first print publication dedicated to cryptocurrency, and won a bronze medal at the International Olympiad in Informatics.

trajectory.title: Published the Ethereum white paper
trajectory.description: Published the Ethereum white paper proposing a Turing-complete blockchain platform that could run smart contracts, going beyond Bitcoin's payment-focused design.

trajectory.title: Awarded Thiel Fellowship and dropped out of university
trajectory.description: Received the Thiel Fellowship ($100,000 for young people under 23 to pursue interests outside academia) and dropped out of the University of Waterloo to work on Ethereum full-time.

trajectory.title: Ethereum blockchain launched
trajectory.description: The Ethereum blockchain was officially launched on July 30, 2015, with the mining of the Genesis block, after a successful crowdsale raised $18 million.

trajectory.title: Became youngest crypto billionaire
trajectory.description: When Ether crossed $3,000 in May 2021, Buterin became the world's youngest crypto billionaire at age 27.

trajectory.title: Ethereum completed 'The Merge'
trajectory.description: Ethereum transitioned from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake in 'The Merge,' reducing the network's energy consumption by 99.95%, a major technical milestone.

name: Alexis Ohanian
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Reddit through Y Combinator
starting_point: Born in Brooklyn, New York to an Armenian-American father and a German-American mother; grew up in the Baltimore area; attended the University of Virginia, studying commerce and history.
current_position: Co-founder of Reddit; venture capitalist and founder of 776; married to Serena Williams; net worth approximately $70 million+; resides in Florida.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Reddit through Y Combinator
trajectory.description: After walking out of the LSAT, co-founded Reddit with college roommate Steve Huffman, accepted into Y Combinator's first batch with the idea of 'the front page of the internet.'

trajectory.title: Sold Reddit to Conde Nast for $10-20 million
trajectory.description: Sold Reddit to Conde Nast Publications for a reported $10-20 million, becoming a millionaire at 23, and remained with the company for three years.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Initialized Capital
trajectory.description: Co-founded the early-stage venture capital firm Initialized Capital with Garry Tan, which became an early backer of Coinbase, Instacart, and Opendoor.

trajectory.title: Returned to Reddit as executive chairman
trajectory.description: Returned to Reddit as executive chairman to lead the company's turnaround, overseeing product and mobile strategy.

trajectory.title: Married Serena Williams
trajectory.description: Married tennis superstar Serena Williams in a high-profile ceremony in New Orleans.

trajectory.title: Left Reddit board and launched 776 fund
trajectory.description: Resigned from Reddit's board of directors, urging the company to replace him with a Black board member, and launched the venture fund 776 to support early-stage founders.

name: Steve Huffman
milestone_by_age_26: Built Reddit as co-founder
starting_point: Born in 1983 or 1984 in Warrenton, Virginia; began programming at age 8; attended the University of Virginia, studying computer science, where he met Alexis Ohanian.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Reddit; net worth approximately $1.2 billion as of November 2025; resides in San Francisco, California.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Reddit and programmed the entire site
trajectory.description: Co-founded Reddit with Alexis Ohanian after being accepted into Y Combinator's first batch, programming the entire site in Lisp and launching it in June 2005.

trajectory.title: Sold Reddit to Conde Nast
trajectory.description: Sold Reddit to Conde Nast for a reported $10-20 million and remained with the company for several years before departing.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Hipmunk
trajectory.description: Co-founded the airfare search engine Hipmunk, which aimed to simplify travel booking with a visual interface, serving as CEO and CTO.

trajectory.title: Returned as CEO of Reddit
trajectory.description: Returned to Reddit as CEO to replace Ellen Pao, leading the company through significant growth and platform evolution.

trajectory.title: Reddit IPO
trajectory.description: Led Reddit through its initial public offering on the New York Stock Exchange in March 2024, valuing the company at approximately $6.4 billion.

name: Drew Houston
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Dropbox and entered YC
starting_point: Born in Acton, Massachusetts; father showed him programming at a young age; attended MIT, studying computer science, where he met co-founder Arash Ferdowsi.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Dropbox; board member of Meta Platforms; net worth approximately $2 billion; transitioning to executive chairman role in 2026.

trajectory.title: Graduated from MIT
trajectory.description: Graduated from MIT with a degree in computer science, having co-founded a SAT prep company during his time there and worked at Bit9 as a software engineer.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Dropbox and entered Y Combinator
trajectory.description: Co-founded Dropbox with MIT classmate Arash Ferdowsi, entering Y Combinator's accelerator program after famously being rejected initially.

trajectory.title: Dropbox launched publicly
trajectory.description: Dropbox launched to the public, quickly gaining millions of users and becoming Y Combinator's most successful investment at the time.

trajectory.title: Dropbox IPO
trajectory.description: Dropbox went public on the Nasdaq, becoming Y Combinator's first startup to ever IPO, valuing the company at over $9 billion.

trajectory.title: Joined Meta board of directors
trajectory.description: Joined the board of directors of Meta Platforms (formerly Facebook), replacing Netflix CEO Reed Hastings.

trajectory.title: Stepping down as CEO of Dropbox
trajectory.description: Announced he would step down as CEO of Dropbox to become executive chairman, serving as co-CEO during a transition period.

name: Sam Altman
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Loopt and entered Y Combinator
starting_point: Born in Chicago, Illinois to a dermatologist mother and a real estate broker father; grew up in St. Louis, Missouri; attended John Burroughs School and Stanford University.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of OpenAI; billionaire investor; one of the most influential figures in the AI industry; resides in San Francisco, California.

trajectory.title: Dropped out of Stanford and co-founded Loopt
trajectory.description: Dropped out of Stanford University after two years to co-found Loopt, a location-based social networking app, in Y Combinator's first batch.

trajectory.title: Sold Loopt for $43.4 million
trajectory.description: Sold Loopt to Green Dot Corporation for $43.4 million, using the proceeds to seed his own venture fund and invest in startups.

trajectory.title: Became president of Y Combinator
trajectory.description: Became president of Y Combinator, the world's leading startup accelerator, at age 28, expanding its scale and influence significantly.

trajectory.title: Co-founded OpenAI
trajectory.description: Co-founded OpenAI with Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever, and others as a non-profit AI research company, initially serving as co-chair.

trajectory.title: Became CEO of OpenAI
trajectory.description: Left Y Combinator to become full-time CEO of OpenAI, transitioning the organization from non-profit to a capped-profit model and raising $1 billion from Microsoft.

trajectory.title: Launched ChatGPT
trajectory.description: Oversaw the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022, which became the fastest-growing consumer application in history and catalyzed the global AI boom.

trajectory.title: Briefly ousted and reinstated as OpenAI CEO
trajectory.description: Was ousted by the OpenAI board in November 2023 for being 'not consistently candid,' but was reinstated as CEO five days later after overwhelming employee and investor support.

name: Neeraj Chopra
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in javelin
starting_point: Born in Khandra village, Panipat district, Haryana, India to farmer parents; grew up in a rural farming family and started javelin throwing at age 14 to get fit.
current_position: Indian javelin thrower; Olympic gold and silver medalist; World Champion; Diamond League winner; Lieutenant Colonel in the Indian Army; India's most prominent track and field athlete.

trajectory.title: Started throwing javelin
trajectory.description: Joined a local sports group to get active and discovered a natural talent for javelin throwing, reaching 40-45 metres within ten days.

trajectory.title: Won World U20 Championships with world record
trajectory.description: Won gold at the World U20 Championships in Bydgoszcz with a throw of 86.48m, setting a world U20 record and becoming the first Indian to win a world athletics title at any level.

trajectory.title: Won Asian Championships
trajectory.description: Won gold at the Asian Athletics Championships, establishing himself as Asia's leading javelin thrower.

trajectory.title: Won gold at Commonwealth and Asian Games
trajectory.description: Won gold at both the Gold Coast Commonwealth Games and the Jakarta Asian Games, becoming a national hero in India.

trajectory.title: Won Olympic gold at Tokyo 2020
trajectory.description: Won gold in javelin at the Tokyo Olympics with a throw of 87.58m, becoming India's first Olympic gold medalist in athletics and only the second Indian to win an individual Olympic gold.

trajectory.title: Won Diamond League final
trajectory.description: Won the Diamond League final, becoming the first Indian to win the prestigious athletics series.

trajectory.title: Won World Championships gold
trajectory.description: Won gold at the World Athletics Championships in Budapest, becoming the first Asian to win a javelin world title.

trajectory.title: Won Olympic silver at Paris 2024
trajectory.description: Won silver in javelin at the Paris Olympics, becoming one of only five individual multiple Olympic medalists for India.

name: Nikola Jokic
milestone_by_age_26: Named the Adriatic (ABA) League regular season MVP in 2014-15 at age 20, averaging 15.4 points and league-leading 9.3 rebounds. Drafted 41st overall by the Denver Nuggets in the 2014 NBA Draft, made the NBA All-Rookie First Team in 2016, and became an NBA All-Star at 24, all before age 26.
starting_point: Born in Sombor, Serbia, FR Yugoslavia to a family with two older brothers 11 and 13 years his senior; introduced to basketball by his brothers; developed an interest in competitive horse racing alongside basketball.
current_position: Center for the Denver Nuggets; three-time NBA MVP; NBA Finals MVP and champion; eight-time NBA All-Star; widely regarded as one of the greatest centers and passers in NBA history.

trajectory.title: Joined KK Mega Basket in Belgrade
trajectory.description: Moved to Belgrade to join the professional team KK Mega Basket of the Adriatic Basketball Association, initially playing for the junior team and being named junior league MVP.

trajectory.title: Drafted 41st overall by Denver Nuggets
trajectory.description: Was selected by the Denver Nuggets with the 41st overall pick in the second round of the 2014 NBA Draft, a pick now considered one of the greatest draft steals in NBA history.

trajectory.title: NBA debut and All-Rookie First Team
trajectory.description: Made his NBA debut in October 2015 and was named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team, quickly establishing himself as a unique playmaking center.

trajectory.title: First NBA All-Star selection
trajectory.description: Was selected as an NBA All-Star for the first time, recognizing his emergence as one of the league's most unique and talented big men.

trajectory.title: Won first NBA MVP award
trajectory.description: Won his first NBA Most Valuable Player award, becoming the lowest-drafted player ever to win MVP and the first Serbian to receive the honor.

trajectory.title: Won second consecutive NBA MVP
trajectory.description: Won his second consecutive NBA MVP award, joining an elite group of back-to-back winners and solidifying his status as the league's best player.

trajectory.title: NBA Finals MVP and championship
trajectory.description: Led the Denver Nuggets to their first-ever NBA championship and was named NBA Finals MVP, averaging a triple-double in the playoffs.

trajectory.title: Won third NBA MVP award
trajectory.description: Won his third NBA MVP award in four seasons, further cementing his legacy as one of the greatest players of his generation.

name: Jimmy Donaldson
milestone_by_age_26: Reached meaningful YouTube scale; later built the MrBeast content machine
starting_point: Born in Wichita, Kansas to military veteran parents; raised in Greenville, North Carolina; parents divorced when he was young; diagnosed with Crohn's disease as a teenager.
current_position: Founder of Beast Industries; most-subscribed YouTube channel with 500M+ subscribers; net worth approximately $2.6 billion; resides in Greenville, North Carolina.

trajectory.title: Started posting YouTube videos as MrBeast6000
trajectory.description: Began posting YouTube videos at age 13, starting with Let's Play gaming content and videos estimating other YouTubers' earnings.

trajectory.title: 'I Counted to 100,000' went viral
trajectory.description: Posted a video of himself counting to 100,000 over 44 hours, which drew tens of thousands of views within days and launched his career in elaborate challenge content.

trajectory.title: Started philanthropic stunt videos
trajectory.description: Began creating videos featuring massive cash giveaways and philanthropic stunts, including donating $10,000 to strangers and tipping pizza delivery drivers $10,000.

trajectory.title: Launched MrBeast Burger
trajectory.description: Launched MrBeast Burger, a virtual restaurant chain that rapidly expanded to hundreds of locations, leveraging his massive YouTube audience for distribution.

trajectory.title: Launched Feastables snack brand
trajectory.description: Launched Feastables, a chocolate bar and snack brand that leveraged his massive audience and quickly achieved widespread retail distribution.

trajectory.title: Became most-subscribed YouTube channel
trajectory.description: Surpassed PewDiePie to become the most-subscribed individual YouTube channel, reaching over 100 million subscribers and continuing rapid growth.

trajectory.title: Launched Beast Games on Prime Video
trajectory.description: Launched 'Beast Games,' a reality competition show on Amazon Prime Video, expanding his content empire beyond YouTube into streaming television.

trajectory.title: Crossed 500 million YouTube subscribers
trajectory.description: Became the first and only YouTuber to cross 500 million subscribers on his main channel, solidifying his position as the platform's biggest creator.

name: Kylie Jenner
milestone_by_age_26: Launched Kylie Lip Kits with immediate large-scale demand
starting_point: Born in Los Angeles, California to Olympic decathlete Caitlyn Jenner and television personality Kris Jenner; youngest of the Kardashian-Jenner family; grew up on reality TV from age 10.
current_position: Founder and owner of Kylie Cosmetics and Khy apparel; reality TV star; one of the most-followed people on Instagram; net worth approximately $700+ million; resides in Hidden Hills, California.

trajectory.title: Began appearing on Keeping Up with the Kardashians
trajectory.description: Began appearing on the E! reality television series Keeping Up with the Kardashians at age 10, building a public profile from childhood.

trajectory.title: Launched Kendall & Kylie clothing line with PacSun
trajectory.description: Collaborated with sister Kendall and clothing brand PacSun to launch the Kendall & Kylie clothing line, gaining early retail experience.

trajectory.title: Launched Kylie Lip Kits
trajectory.description: Launched Kylie Lip Kits with three shades priced at $29 each, with 15,000 units selling out in under one minute, crashing the website and proving massive demand.

trajectory.title: Rebranded to Kylie Cosmetics and expanded product line
trajectory.description: Renamed Kylie Lip Kits to Kylie Cosmetics and expanded into a full cosmetics line including eyeshadows, highlighters, and makeup brushes.

trajectory.title: Kylie Cosmetics crossed $420 million in retail sales
trajectory.description: By June 2017, Kylie Cosmetics had crossed $420 million in retail sales, an extraordinary growth trajectory for a celebrity beauty brand.

trajectory.title: Sold 51% of Kylie Cosmetics to Coty for $600 million
trajectory.description: Sold a 51% majority stake in Kylie Cosmetics to Coty Inc. for $600 million, valuing the brand at $1.2 billion, though Forbes later revoked her 'billionaire' title after investigating actual revenues.

trajectory.title: First woman to reach 300 million Instagram followers
trajectory.description: Became the first woman to reach 300 million followers on Instagram, cementing her status as one of the most influential social media figures in the world.

trajectory.title: Launched Khy apparel line
trajectory.description: Launched Khy, a 12-piece apparel line inspired by her personal style, expanding her business empire beyond cosmetics into fashion.

name: Richard Stallman
milestone_by_age_26: Developed Emacs, the first extensible customizable self-documenting display editor, at the MIT AI Lab in 1976 (age 23), and published the EMACS paper as MIT AI Memo 519 in June 1979 (age 26).
starting_point: Born in New York City to a printing brokerage operator father and a teacher mother; grew up in a Jewish family with an early interest in computers, attending Columbia University's Saturday program for high school students.
current_position: Founder of the GNU Project and the Free Software Foundation; free software movement activist; programmer; resides in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

trajectory.title: Joined the MIT AI Lab
trajectory.description: Began working as a programmer at the MIT Artificial Intelligence Lab while an undergraduate at Harvard, joining the legendary hacker culture of the PDP-10 era.

trajectory.title: Developed Emacs
trajectory.description: Created Emacs, the first extensible, customizable, self-documenting display editor, at the MIT AI Lab, revolutionizing text editing and establishing the concept of programmable software tools.

trajectory.title: Launched the GNU Project
trajectory.description: Announced the GNU Project to create a Unix-like operating system composed entirely of free software, launching the free software movement.

trajectory.title: Left MIT to work on GNU full-time
trajectory.description: Resigned from MIT employment to dedicate himself full-time to the GNU Project, developing GNU Emacs and other free software components.

trajectory.title: Founded the Free Software Foundation
trajectory.description: Established the Free Software Foundation (FSF) in October 1985 to support the free software movement and the GNU Project.

trajectory.title: Wrote the GNU General Public License v1
trajectory.description: Authored the first version of the GNU General Public License (GPL), a revolutionary copyright license that ensured software freedom through copyleft.

trajectory.title: Won Grace Murray Hopper Award and MacArthur Fellowship
trajectory.description: Received the ACM Grace Murray Hopper Award for pioneering work on Emacs and was awarded a MacArthur Fellowship in the same year.

trajectory.title: Resigned as FSF president
trajectory.description: Resigned as president of the Free Software Foundation and left his MIT visiting scientist role amid controversy over comments related to the Jeffrey Epstein scandal.
